A parameter reversal sends (E,L) to (-E,-L), so it cannot make E>0 and L>=0 for a ray with L/E<0. This is a fatal logical overclaim. Kept both angular directions by retaining signed L and defining b=|L|/E; the radial first integral depends on L squared and its threshold is unchanged.

The energy-trapping and one-sided escape arguments establish the stated threshold, but their unscaled Euclidean balls mix length and speed. This is a nonfatal dimensional-coordinate omission. Specified SI and dimensionless (r/s,w/c,c*tau/s), with energy bounds c^2*epsilon^2/8, perturbations s*delta/2, and escape radius eta/s; all three classifications are preserved.

Also closed the digest logarithm concern using derivative-zero/MVT proofs of the quotient and square laws and the integral remainder identity.

Specified SI s,r,b,bc as lengths, H as inverse squared length and b^2H as dimensionless, retaining the same exact turning and critical-ray claims.
